historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: continuing-operations growth after the FY2027 perimeter step-down (base path years 2-10 average ~2.7%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (8.5% / 6.4%) is NOT organic: shareholders' equity went 42,110 (FY2023) -> 15,568 (FY2025) -> 53,784 (FY2026) through a 24.3bn loss, then a 20.0bn capital injection, a 12.0bn debt waiver and 23.7bn of asset-sale gains. EPS CAGRs are undefined (negative FY2023/FY2024/FY2025 EPS, and FY2026 EPS is one-off driven). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR undefined (FY2023 owner FCF -7,449); 5yr -16.5% (8,161 -> 3,309) reflects the crisis years, not the post-exit business. None of the historical CAGRs is a usable forward anchor; the forward path is built from FY2027 guidance, Q1 FY2027 actuals and segment margins instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF == reported FCF throughout (SBC zero; interest income 36-166m/yr not stripped because the company was net-debt in every year). Reported FCF series (OCF - capex, JPY m): FY2021 8,161; FY2022 561; FY2023 -7,449; FY2024 1,498; FY2025 2,406; FY2026 3,309 -- FY2026 is depressed by a 5,304 pension settlement and 9.7bn of restructuring charges partly paid in cash, and flattered by 7.7bn of receivables release from exited businesses.

scenario_narratives.base: The restructuring is complete and the continuing company -- Polymers (nylon/PET film, engineering plastics) plus Functional Materials (glass cloth, activated carbon fibre, glass beads) with a residual monofilament business -- settles at ~88bn of FY2027 revenue and a 14-14.5% EBITDA margin: well above the 11.7% FY2026 margin on the old perimeter because the loss-making fibre/nonwoven units are gone, but below the 17.3% Q1 FY2027 print because the AI-substrate glass-cloth premium normalises and feedstock costs are only partly passed through. Capex is rebuilt to 4.5-5% of revenue after two starved years, cash taxes ramp to the statutory 31% as the NOL shield runs off, and value accrues to a fully diluted 519.7m shares because REVIC's C-class preferred converts 4-for-1 at ~JPY 43.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI/data-centre substrate cycle proves multi-year: ultra-thin low-CTE glass cloth and electronics-grade nylon film grow high-single-digits for four years, the Q1 FY2027 17% operating margin becomes the norm (17.5% EBITDA), and management funds capacity at 5.5-6% of revenue. A 14x terminal cap credits a specialty-materials multiple. The share count is still fully diluted -- the bull case does not assume REVIC leaves the conversion right unexercised.
scenario_narratives.bear: Revenue lands on the 84bn guide and then shrinks another 2% as stranded industrial-textile lines are exited; the glass-cloth cycle turns in FY2028 just as oil-linked feedstock and energy costs rise, and the EBITDA margin falls back to 10% -- the FY2021-22 level of the old Polymers-led business. Growth is 0-1%, the terminal multiple is capped at 10x, and the unfunded pension and wind-down provisions remain cash claims. Covenant or solvency failure is NOT assumed (equity ratio 38.6%, net debt ~1x EBITDA), which is why this is a bear case rather than the receivership waterfall.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A normalised, post-restructuring owner-FCF DCF on the fully diluted share count. The two judgments that matter most are (1) treating the REVIC C-class preferred as 462m common shares -- it converts at ~JPY 43 and is therefore worth its converted value, not its JPY 20bn paid-in capital, so the common owns 11% of the equity -- and (2) refusing to capitalise FY2026's one-off-driven profit or Q1 FY2027's record margin, instead building FY2027 from guidance and segment margins and fading the AI glass-cloth premium. Both push value far below a quote that was set during a retail/short-covering rally and that appears to price the common as if it were the only equity claim.
key_risks_to_valuation: C-class terms: the issuance 発行要領 is not in the extracted filings. If the preferred carried a company cash-redemption right at paid-in value that REVIC could not pre-empt by converting, the dilution would shrink from 462m shares to zero and per-share value would rise ~8x less a JPY 20bn deduction; the 4-for-1 dilutive count the company itself reports in two consecutive filings makes this unlikely but it is the single largest swing factor.

Normalisation call on margins: Q1 FY2027 OP margin was 17.3% against a 14.5% base EBITDA margin (OP ~11%); if the AI-substrate glass-cloth premium is structural rather than cyclical, the bull case is the base case.
Perimeter: revenue guidance of 84bn vs a 96bn Q1 run-rate leaves ~12bn of FY2027 revenue whose fate (exit vs retention) is unclear; the base splits the difference.
Cash taxes: the NOL position after the FY2026 gains is not disclosed in the tanshin; a fuller shield would add value in years 1-3, an 8.5bn deferred tax liability crystallising would subtract it.
Price anchor: 52-week range JPY 186-4,380 on a thematic retail narrative; upside/downside and entry-price gaps are against a quote with no fundamental anchor.
REVIC exit path: a block sale or conversion-and-placement of the C-class could reset the share register and the price regardless of operating results.
Pension and wind-down claims (JPY 7.1bn unfunded retirement obligation, 0.7bn provisions) are in the bridge at book; further stranded costs from residual fibre exits are not.

inputs.share_count_basis: FULLY DILUTED per the company's own diluted-EPS note (FY2026 tanshin lines 814-821 and Q1 FY2027): 57,654k weighted common + 462,018k common issuable on conversion of the 115,504,600 C-class preferred shares held by REVIC (a fixed 4-for-1 conversion; the dilutive count is identical in FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 despite very different share prices, so the ratio is not market-linked). Issue price was JPY 173.16 per preferred = JPY 43.29 per common on conversion, so the conversion is deeply in the money at any price above ~JPY 45 and REVIC (66.76% of votes, controls the board) or any buyer of its stake would convert rather than hold a JPY 20.0bn liquidation preference. The common therefore owns 57.654/519.672 = 11.1% of the economic equity. Held FLAT (no SBC; no other dilutive instruments disclosed). The exact 発行要領 (put/call dates, any cash-redemption right) is not in the extracted filings -- see notes.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment line in the FY2026 consolidated cash-flow statement or notes (J-GAAP tanshin, 3103.T_Annual_FY2025.txt lines 600-662); Japanese Standard-market industrial with no stock-option programme disclosed. SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-denominated flows discounted at a JPY-built rate: JGB 10y ~1.6% + ~5.5% Japan ERP x beta ~1.2 gives ~8.2% cost of equity; small-cap/Standard-market illiquidity takes it to ~9%. Debt is ~11% of diluted market value at ~3% pre-tax, so WACC rounds to 9.0% -- the house reference for JPY industrials. Risk is charged ONCE: the turnaround, controlling-shareholder and glass-cloth-cycle risks live in the scenario paths and the 30% bear weight, not in a WACC premium, and WACC is identical across scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases as debt: JPY 2,576m of finance-lease liabilities (501 current + 2,075 non-current, 31 Mar 2026; Q1 folds them into 'other') added to total_debt; lease principal (inside financing 'other', ~JPY 0.6bn) is NOT deducted from the flows. J-GAAP operating leases are already expensed in EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at book (JPY 269m, 30 Jun 2026); flows are consolidated. NCI is 0.5% of equity so the attributable-vs-consolidated distinction is immaterial.
inputs.net_debt_detail: 30 Jun 2026: borrowings 12,964 short-term + 28,593 current LTD + 13,117 LTD = 54,674; + finance leases 2,576 (31 Mar 2026 figure) = total_debt 57,250. Cash & deposits 45,197 (includes ~JPY 0.4bn of >3-month deposits that the CF statement excludes from equivalents; treated as cash). Net debt 12,053. Cash fell JPY 2.5bn in Q1 largely because ~JPY 4.0bn of corporate tax on the FY2026 asset-sale gains was paid (tax payable 4,521 -> 465).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income JPY 166m is NOT stripped: the company is net-DEBT (12.1bn), so the cash pile is not being added to EV and there is no double count. Interest received and the ~JPY 136m of dividends received stay in reported OCF; the investment-securities portfolio they partly derive from is added to the bridge at book (3,118), which is a small, deliberate asymmetry disclosed here.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (house default for an operating company), with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (JPY WACC, leases-as-debt, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule, SBC-zero). ROUTING: Unitika is a going-concern specialty-materials manufacturer that has COMPLETED a REVIC/MUFG-led financial restructuring (Apr 2025 JPY 20.0bn C-class placement, JPY 12,015m bank debt forgiveness booked FY2026, exits from clothing fibre/nonwovens/most industrial fibre 'substantially complete' per management); equity ratio 38.6% and net debt ~1x EBITDA at 30 Jun 2026. It is therefore NOT the 'distressed/receivership -> asset waterfall' row: there is a forward cash-flow stream to discount. The distressed history is handled through (i) a NORMALISED base year rather than FY2026 actuals, (ii) an explicit year-1 revenue step-down to the post-exit perimeter, (iii) a 30% bear weight, and (iv) debt-like restructuring and pension claims in the bridge. BASE YEAR: FY2026 revenue (118,563) is only the compounding base; FY2026 net income (18,153) and OCF are NOT used -- they carry a 23,697 gain on fixed-asset sales, the 12,015 debt-forgiveness gain, 9,727 of structural-improvement costs and a 5,304 pension settlement. The year-1 (FY2027) path is built from FY2027 guidance (revenue 84,000 / OP 8,000 / NI 5,000, reaffirmed 6 Aug 2026) and the Q1 FY2027 actuals (revenue 24,108, OP 4,162 = 17.3% margin, a record): base takes revenue 88bn (between the 84bn guide and the 96bn Q1 run-rate, allowing for further H2 roll-off) and a 14.5% EBITDA margin (OP ~9.6bn, above the 8.0bn guide which management itself describes as held for feedstock-cost caution with a 52% Q1 progress rate). Segment check: FY2026 Polymers OP margin 16.7% (9,429/56,395), Functional Materials 4.8%, Fibres loss -- the post-exit mix is roughly 65/35 Polymers/Functional Materials, so a 14-15% consolidated EBITDA margin is a mid-cycle view that already fades the AI glass-cloth boost. CAPEX/D&A: FY2025-26 capex (3.1%, 1.9% of revenue) was crisis-starved against a 5.6-7.7% FY2020-24 history; base normalises to 4.5-5.0% with D&A rising from 3.6% to 4.0% of the smaller revenue base. CASH TAX: statutory ~31%; the capital reduction to JPY 100m (Apr 2025) qualifies Unitika for 100% NOL offset, but ~JPY 4.5bn of current tax accrued on FY2026 (14% of 31.9bn pre-tax) and an 8.5bn deferred tax liability show the shield is partial, so the cash rate ramps 20% -> 31% by year 4 rather than starting near zero. WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer (receivables + inventory > payables), so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-10% of the revenue change): the year-1 perimeter contraction releases ~JPY 3bn of residual working capital from units still exiting during FY2027, later growth consumes cash. Capture is held below the ~15% a manufacturer of this kind normally carries because FY2026 already released 7.7bn of receivables and 3.0bn of inventory and the businesses SOLD in FY2026 took their working capital with them, so a full 15% on the FY2027 step-down would double-count; the year-1 owner-FCF margin (~12%) is therefore above the steady-state ~6% for this one-off reason and should not be read as a run-rate. PREFERRED: valued on the fully diluted 519.7m count with NO deduction for the JPY 20.0bn C-class paid-in capital (on conversion it is common equity) and the JPY 262-367m/yr C-class coupon (2.27 -> 3.18 per preferred share) is ignored as it disappears on conversion. If the C-class were instead treated as JPY 20.0bn of debt and NOT converted, common-only value per BASIC share would be (diluted equity value - 20,000) / 57.654m, i.e. roughly 8-9x the diluted per-share figures below less ~JPY 347/share -- the market price appears to be set on something close to that basic-share basis, which is the central disagreement between this valuation and the quote. TERMINAL: Gordon at 9%/1.5% is 13.5x; the 12x cap binds in base (cyclical materials, 12-15x range per method; Unitika's own pre-crisis EV/EBITDA was ~5-8x so even 12x embeds a re-rating). HORIZON 10 years so the capex/D&A/tax paths mature before capitalisation. BAND: house and street coincide (SBC zero) -- band_position is degenerate and should be read as n/a. PRICE: TSE regular close; the stock traded JPY 186-4,380 over 52 weeks on a retail AI-glass-cloth theme, so entry-price and upside framing are against an unusually unstable anchor.

bear.growth_rates_note: Year 1 = FY2027 revenue at the 84.0bn guide; further stranded-business shrinkage in year 2, then a flat-to-1% Japanese materials business.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: Glass-cloth cycle turns in FY2028 and feedstock/energy costs are not passed through; EBITDA margin settles at 10% (OP ~6%), roughly the FY2021-22 pre-crisis level.

base.growth_rates_note: Year 1 = FY2027 revenue ~88.0bn (guide 84.0bn, Q1 run-rate 96.4bn); years 2-10 continuing-ops growth from glass cloth / high-value films fading to Japan nominal GDP.
base.ebitda_margin_note: FY2027 OP ~9.6bn (guide 8.0bn, Q1 4.16bn); fades 0.5pp from year 4 as the AI glass-cloth cycle normalises. FY2026 actual EBITDA margin 11.7% on the pre-exit perimeter.

bull.growth_rates_note: Year 1 = FY2027 revenue ~92.5bn (less H2 roll-off than guided); glass-cloth capacity additions and electronics-grade film drive high-single-digit growth to year 4.
bull.ebitda_margin_note: Q1 FY2027's 17.3% OP margin proves durable as the mix shifts to semiconductor-substrate glass cloth; EBITDA margin reaches 17.5% (OP ~13%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 30/50/20. Bear up to 30%: the thesis rests on a turnaround that is one year old, the margin evidence is two quarters of a cyclical AI-materials boom, the equity cushion has never been tested through a downturn, and a controlling shareholder (REVIC, 66.8% of votes) with a public-recovery mandate rather than a long-horizon owner. Bull down to 20%: it needs the glass-cloth cycle to persist AND the record Q1 margin to hold AND capacity to be funded, three independent things.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
